reason: E1 states that severe lattice distortion causes low atomic diffusivity and that high configurational entropy stabilizes the solid-solution phase, supporting the first two premises. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides any evidence that SRO can be induced by annealing, that SRO increases diffusion barriers, or that SRO improves high-temperature stability; these central mechanistic premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Near-equiatomic HEA nanoparticles exhibit low atomic diffusivity due to severe lattice distortion
High configurational entropy stabilizes the solid-solution phase against phase segregation
Short-range chemical ordering (SRO) can be induced by post-synthesis annealing
SRO increases local energy barriers for atomic migration, reducing diffusion and sintering
Enhanced SRO leads to improved structural and chemical stability at high temperatures
